_comment: Routing table: which of Zoinkity's 617 notes is AUTHORITATIVE for a given
question, and which source files each area governs.
This exists because searching 617 files is a decision, and under momentum
the decision does not get made - four times in one session, at a cost of
hours, when each lookup would have taken under a minute. The table turns
'which doc covers this?' from judgement into a lookup.
GROW THIS. Every time a doc answers a question, add the mapping. Every time
the docs are searched and found silent, add it to 'not_covered' so nobody
re-searches a dead end.
Authority warning: 'Rand++ Documentation (Misc)/' documents a ROM HACK's
modified formats, not the base game. Never cite it as authority.
docs_root below is INTENTIONALLY EMPTY. gedocs.py resolves the notes in
this order: $GEDOCS_DOCS_ROOT, then the value below IF IT IS SET AND THAT
PATH EXISTS, then ../goldeneye_docs/notes/GE Documentation beside this
repo. Leaving it empty means the sibling rule decides, which is the rule
that actually holds on Windows, WSL and Linux alike.
It previously recorded an absolute pre-migration path. Measured 2026-09-01:
that path still exists under WSL and is at the SAME COMMIT as the canonical
checkout, so it was serving identical content and nothing was wrong today.
It was a latent trap, not an active bug - the pre-migration copy is kept
deliberately frozen as a safety reference, so it would have outranked the
canonical sibling the first time the canonical copy moved ahead.
Do not put a machine's absolute path here. Set $GEDOCS_DOCS_ROOT instead.

the authority on what 'untextured' means in a list. Gives the two patterns side by side: textured is BA 2-cycle + FC26A004 1F1093FF + BB002801, untextured is BA 1-cycle + FCFFFFFF FFFE793C + BB000001. display-lists.learned:
2026-08-24: the collision-DL crash was an opcode read from byte 0 of a list sl_gfx_dl_swap had already rewritten to NATIVE word order (opcode is byte 3 on x86). Two source-reading theories were wrong; ucode05.txt settled it. From the same file, for the parser conversion: opcodes 04=vertex, B1=GE_TRI4 (Rare's four-triangle command in F3DEX's G_TRI2 slot, explicitly NOT F3DEX format), BF=tri1, B8=enddl, B9/BA=setothermode_l/h. tri4 indices are nibbles 0-F packed across both words; the vertex buffer is 16 entries because only 0-F is addressable; all-zero triangles are skipped; and triangles REQUIRE a vertex offset set by the vertex command - the precondition the crash violated.  2026-08-25, the 2D command set (E4 texrect + B3/B4 rdphalf, F6 fillrect, F7/F8/FA/FB colour registers, FC setcombine, B6/B7 geometry mode, FF/FE image pointers): ucode05.txt covers all of them EXCEPT FC, which it sends to SETCOMBINE.HTM - not in the corpus, and ucode05_old.txt carries the table, the same fallback that already worked for F5 settile and B9/BA setothermode. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE NOTES, both measured against a live Facility frame. (1) ucode05.txt's E4 entry has its corner labels transposed: it calls the upper word 'upper left' and the lower word 'lower right', but 225 of 225 texrects in one frame put the LARGER coordinate in w0, which is its own E5 entry's labelling and gbi.h's packing. (2) A texrect is three 64-bit commands, not one 128-bit one - E4, then B4 with s/t, then B3 with dsdx/dtdy - and the three fixed-point scales differ: rectangle 10.2, s/t 10.5, dsdx/dtdy s5.10. Also load-bearing and stated nowhere in the notes: F6 fillrect takes the fill-colour register ONLY in FILL cycle type; in 1-cycle it goes through the colour combiner, which is how GoldenEye draws its menu scrims and level fades (textrelated.c:181 draw_blackbox_to_screen). 2026-08-25, B-021 - A THIRD CORRECTION TO THE NOTES, and the one that was costing character models: ucode05.txt's Rare vertex table gives 'upper 000FFFFF number of bytes to grab', reading bits 16-19 as the top nibble of a 20-bit length. Bits 16-19 are actually v0, the DESTINATION SLOT in the 16-entry vertex buffer. The note's reading is indistinguishable from the truth whenever v0 == 0, which is most of the time. Authority is include/PR/gbi.h:1865, the plain-F3D branch this build compiles (neither F3DEX_GBI nor F3DEX_GBI_2 is defined - build.sh DEFS, and a tree-wide grep finds them only inside gbi.h/gs2dex.h/sptask.h's own ifdefs): gSPVertex(pkt,v,n,v0) = gDma1p(pkt,G_VTX,v,sizeof(Vtx)*(n),((n)-1)<<4|(v0)), and gDma1p puts that byte at bits 16-23 - so 20-23 are n-1 and 16-19 are v0. Settled by measurement, since note and header disagreed: on a streets frame with guards, 513 of 513 vertex commands had (w0 & 0xffff) == n*16 but only 476 had the 20-bit field equal, and the 37 that differed were exactly the 37 carrying a non-zero bits 16-19 - and exactly the 37 the old length check rejected. Facility and dam measure 0, which is why an earlier '3360 of 3360' check on those two levels looked clean. ALSO from B-021, and stated nowhere in the notes: the RSP transforms a vertex WHEN THE 04 LOADS IT, with the modelview then in effect, and a later 01 does not re-transform what is already loaded. That is how GoldenEye deforms a limb with no matrix stack at all - dotube (model.c:4683-4686) loads a tube's proximal ring under one bone matrix and the rest under the next bone's. Corollary: push=0/pop=0 is CORRECT for this game, not a bug - G_MTX_PUSH and gSPPopMatrix appear nowhere in src/ (tree-wide grep empty), because bone hierarchy is composed on the CPU into model->render_pos (model.c:1783) and issued as absolute LOAD|NOPUSH matrices. 2026-08-26, B-035: the in-game health ring drew at 8/255 of its correct hue because tex_apply gated 3D texturing on BB's enable byte alone. 'Texture application (Rooms).txt' settles it in one line - untextured room geometry is spelled BB000001 (ON, level 0) plus FCFFFFFF FFFE793C, so BB is never the gate and a list that issues no BB of its own inherits the previous draw's tile. The gauge (gDPSetCombineMode G_CC_SHADE, bondview2.c:8617) sets exactly that FC and emits only gSPVertex/gSP2Triangles. This CORRECTS B-034 hypothesis 1, which had the first half right ('level is not a texture gate') and then concluded no triangle draws under a texel-free combiner - false, and measured on the submitted stream rather than on the renderer. Live per-frame counts with the gate armed: dam 34, streets 68, statue 56, archives 3, facility 0. Only four texel-free combiners appear across the twenty-level sweep plus the watch path, all of the same family: fcffffff fffe793c (SHADE/SHADE, the note's own pattern), fffe7838 (1-cycle sibling), fffe7b3d (colour SHADE, alpha ENVIRONMENT), fffdf6fb (PRIM/PRIM, watch menu). 2026-08-26, B-046: THREE more things the combiner table settles that the renderer had guessed at. (1) ucode05_old.txt's FC table is the authority on the c mux being FIVE bits (0x1f at bit 15) while a/b/d are four and three: 8..15 in the b mux and 7 in the d mux are the constant ZERO, which is what makes (X - 0) * K + 0 recognisable as an ordinary modulate. The renderer recognised only the ZERO-MULTIPLIER shape (c >= 16, output exactly d) and drew every modulate as plain white, discarding PRIMITIVE and ENVIRONMENT everywhere - the death blood overlay (fc119623 ff2fffff =(TEXEL0-0)*PRIM+0 over a 4-bit INTENSITY image, prim 96 00 00 b4 measured byte for byte against blood_animation.c:266) and the boot-logo fade-in (same combiner, 260 triangles, prim ramping 000000 to 100e10 over six frames). (2) The explosion colour is NOT in a colour register at all: all fifteen lists in assets/oddtextures.c set G_CC_INTERFERENCE = TEXEL0 * TEXEL1 in 2-cycle and load an IA smoke frame into tile 0 and an RGBA16 FIRE frame into tile 1, so a renderer that binds one texture gets a white smokeball by construction. Measured live as fc111404 ff13ffff. (3) ucode05.txt's '03 rsp_uc05_movemem' type 0x80 viewport is NOT ignorable for one player: GoldenEye renders into a 320x220 letterbox, measured every frame on statue/dam/facility as scale=(640,440) trans=(640,480) -> x[0,320] y[10,230] of 320x240, and its full-screen overlays cover exactly that (fillrect y[10.0,231.0]). Dropping the viewport stretched all 3D by 240/220 and let the world draw over the letterbox, which reads as 'the overlay has gaps' when the overlay is correct and the world is too tall. ALSO settled here, for the boot logos: geometry mode seen=001f3205 carries G_LIGHTING (0x20000) and G_TEXTURE_GEN (0x40000) and movemem uploads G_MV_L0/G_MV_L1, so the Vtx cn[] bytes there are NORMALS, not colours - reading them as colours is what makes the logos a smooth rainbow that follows surface orientation. 2026-08-26, B-044 - a FOURTH correction, and this one is about what the RDP does NOT draw. gbi.h:4602 (the plain-F3D branch this build compiles) packs the E4 texrect's xh/yh - the LOWER RIGHT corner - into w0 and xl/yl into w1, which is the labelling ucode05.txt has transposed (already recorded above, 225 of 225 measured). What follows from it and was NOT recorded: an inverted rectangle draws NOTHING, because the RDP rasterises spans from uly down to lry and lry < uly is zero spans. GoldenEye emits inverted texrects on purpose-built-wrong input - textRenderGlyph's bottom-clip branch (textrelated.c:333) computes lry as `clipY + clipHeight + text_y` and omits the * 4 that every other coordinate in the same command carries, so a glyph straddling the bottom edge of a text clip box arrives as lry=200 against uly=776. Measured on a facility watch capture: 45 such commands, 9 per frame (the nine letters of DETONATOR) on exactly 5 frames, all with w0 y=200 and w1 y=776. draw_texrect's min/max corner normalisation turned each into a valid 144-pixel-tall rect, and with dtdy=1024 over a ~10px glyph the texture tiled ~14 times down it - which is the whole artefact. Rejecting the inverted command restores hardware behaviour; the game's arithmetic is Rare's and stays untouched. 2026-08-26, B-048: the F5 setile LOWER WORD's shift fields, which this file's F5 entry lists as a field table but does not break out - shiftt is 0x00003C00 and shifts is 0x0000000F. Authority is include/PR/gbi.h:3401 gDPSetTile, which packs _SHIFTL(shiftt,10,4) and _SHIFTL(shifts,0,4), and the explosion display lists in assets/oddtextures.c are its own emitter. Values 0..10 shift the incoming s/t RIGHT; 11..15 shift LEFT by 16-shift, and only right shifts occur in this game (measured: odd-shift=0 on every frame that draws one). This is LOAD-BEARING and had been dropped entirely: an explosion's fire tile is F5 line=4 tmem=392 shifts/shiftt=2 with F2 s[0,220] t[0,220], i.e. a settilesize of 56x56 over a loadblock of 224 texels. The two only reconcile through the shift - 56>>2 = 14 texels of real image, on a row stride of line*4 = 16, so the fire is 14 columns padded to 16 for tmem's 8-byte rows. Sizing that tile from settilesize the way tile_texture does is wrong by 4x in both axes. Also measured the same day, on the twenty-level boot sweep plus two explosion replays: twenty distinct combiners reach a draw, ELEVEN name TEXEL1, and exactly ONE is a product - fc111404 ff13ffff, the explosion. The other ten are all (TEXEL1 - TEXEL0) * LODFRAC + TEXEL0 (or PRIMLOD), the 2-cycle mip chain, where TEXEL1 is the next LOD level rather than a second image. 2026-08-28, B9 setothermode_l SHAPES, settled by census over 7300 frames rather than inferred: the game emits exactly TWO shapes - sft=3/len=29 (gDPSetRenderMode, which carries a COMPLETE othermode_l value) and sft=0/len=2 (gDPSetAlphaCompare). Masking the render-mode write field-wise strips bits 0-2, the alpha-compare field, so G_AC_DITHER becomes unreachable - 0050004b was never once observed, only 00500048. The ONLY word in the whole game carrying ac=3 is that render-mode word; explicit gDPSetAlphaCompare fires 8 times and is ALWAYS G_AC_NONE, and the 17 render-mode words carrying ac=0 are what actively CLEAR dither, which is what keeps quiet surfaces clean. Two rival readings were REFUTED by consequence, not argued away: masking field-wise makes dither unreachable while the cartridge visibly dithers; ORing the data in unmasked predicts dither persisting onto the page-select bars drawn next under G_RM_XLU_SURF, and those bars measure 0.38-0.68x the dithered face's frame-to-frame difference, never at or above 1, so they show it THROUGH rather than being cut out. The implemented rule is therefore NARROW - only sft==3 && len==29 takes the whole word, every other shape keeps the field-wise write, so gDPSetAlphaCompare and gDPSetDepthSource still touch only their own fields. The BEHAVIOUR is measured; the microcode-level REASON is not established. See B-056. 2026-09-02, B-077 - the TMEM ADDRESS UNIT, settled by the corpus and needed by anything that addresses inside a load. ucode05_old.txt's `F5 rdp_settile` upper word gives tmem as `0x000001FF` - NINE bits, 512 units across the RDP's texture memory, so one unit is a 64-bit word and a tile sitting `d` units into a load holds the source bytes `d * 8` in. The same entry's lower word carries `0x0003C000 mask t` and `0x000000F0 mask s`, the exponents the RDP wraps s/t at. Corroborated by the game's OWN generator, `images text and font/7F076D68 - generate DL for ImgDecl.txt`: line 985 steps `tmem += tilesize` once per mip level, where tilesize is height * width-rounded-up-to-a-word (:864/:884/:904/:924 per depth) and that same rounded width is written as the F5 `line`; it also sets mask s / mask t to `nearest root to width / height`, i.e. ceil(log2(dim)). One F3 covers the WHOLE chain - texGetDepthAndSize (src/game/tex.c:358) sums every lod into the single length gDPLoadBlock receives (tex.c:514). MEASURED consequence on Facility, and the reason this matters less than it looks: the renderer binds G_TX_RENDERTILE only, that tile is always at the load's own start, and 241654 of 241654 resolutions in a 400-frame windowed run were exact-start - so B-052's interior case is real but never reached by consumed output, and 2^mask equals the renderer's divisor on every REPEATING axis (the six NPOT tiles that disagree are clamped on exactly the disagreeing axis). 2026-09-03, B-088 - A FIFTH CORRECTION TO THE NOTES, and the one that was costing the Rareware logo its material. ucode05_old.txt's F2 entry (:901) says 'Sets size of image to be mapped' and gives width=(lrs-uls)/4+1, height=(lrt-ult)/4+1. That is the CLAMP RECTANGLE, not the image extent, and reading it as the extent is wrong on any axis that REPEATS: the RDP wraps a repeating axis at 2^mask and samples the whole of that span. The mask fields themselves ARE in the corpus and had simply never been read by this renderer - the same F5 lower-word table B-048 took its shifts from carries '0003C000 mask t' and '000000F0 mask s' (ucode05_old.txt:972,:976), bit for bit what include/PR/gbi.h:3415 gsDPSetTile packs as _SHIFTL(maskt,14,4) and _SHIFTL(masks,4,4); G_TX_CLAMP is 0x2 at gbi.h:393. The two readings are indistinguishable whenever the F2 span already equals 2^mask, which is every repeating axis in Facility - B-077 measured exactly that, and it is a fact about Facility, not about the RDP. MEASURED where they disagree: the Rareware logo's D_02004758 (assets/rarewarelogo.c:1245) issues gsDPSetTileSize(0, 46, 116, 124, 124) over a tile title.c:363 loaded with gDPLoadTextureBlock(..., RGBA, 16b, 32, 32, 0, G_TX_WRAP, G_TX_WRAP, 5, 5, ...), so the F2 span is 20x3 while cms=cmt=WRAP with masks=maskt=5 means the RDP wraps at 32x32. 242 of the logo's 260 triangles were therefore sampling a three-texel-tall strip of a 32x32 environment map - shape and texture present, material finish wrong. Corroborated independently by the tile's own declared row stride: line=8 is 64 bytes is 32 texels at 16bpp, and the stride-disagreement census went 1 -> 0 when the width became 32. Containment measured rather than argued: the resize counter is 0 across LEGAL and NINTENDO and 0 in BOTH arms on Facility (identical 1026 textured tris, 27 distinct textures), and first becomes non-zero inside the Rareware window at exactly 242 per frame. 2026-09-03, B-089 - THE ROUTING TABLE HAD NO ENTRY FOR title.c ('no mapped area governs src/game/title.c'), and the operand layout it needed was already here: ucode05.txt's 04 vertex entry gives the lower word as '0f000000 segment / 00ffffff offset in point table'. title.c builds the EYE_INTRO gun-barrel aperture AT RUNTIME - createGunbarrelRenderHole (title3.c:15) writes 30 Vtx_t records, sub_GAME_7F01BFF8 (title3.c:75) wraps them in gSPVertex + gSP1Triangle - and handed the vertex operand as `barrelDisplayListPtr + 0x80000000`, a KSEG0->PHYSICAL conversion spelled as a 32-bit wrap-around ADD instead of through OS_K0_TO_PHYSICAL, so B-019's native fix to those macros never reached it. On the cartridge it is correct because segment 0 is left at 0 and the RSP resolves segment 0 + offset to the RDRAM address behind the KSEG0 pointer; natively there is one flat space and no segment to subtract through. MEASURED on one windowed run: the list carried '04f00100 a00de470' for vertices living at 0x200de470, dl_operand() returned NULL for all 4 vertex batches every frame (vtx=0, unres=4) while the 56 triangles naming them still executed against a vertex buffer nothing had loaded - so the aperture was drawn every frame, degenerate. This is the ONLY hand-rolled address conversion of its kind: `grep -rn "+ *0x80000000" src/` finds that line and nothing else. The carry-forward is not the arithmetic but WHERE it hid - a display list the game BUILDS at runtime is exactly where an address-space assumption survives, because nothing in the asset pipeline byte-swaps or relocates it on the way in, and every earlier sweep had been over lists that arrive from ROM.
  2026-09-08, the Dam sky. ucode05.txt's B2/B3/B4 entries are the AUTHORITY for GoldenEye's hand-built RDP commands, and the B2 entry names the caller outright: "rsp_uc05_rdphalf_cont ... Used by sky and water generators in GE. Follows B4 rdphalf_1 command. Acts as an indicator that the command continues with the given lower word. This is used only when operators longer than 64bits are in use." Its worked example assembles B4/B2 pairs into an 0xCE (G_TRI_SHADE_TXTR, gbi.h:219) triangle - which is exactly what src/game/sky.c emits and what this interpreter was discarding. THE MEASUREMENT that found it: SL_DL_CENSUS=1 on a dam boot reported `sl_ops: top: B2=19` and `orphan-halves=21` every frame with `texrect cmds=0`, i.e. 40 words dropped, and 40 is exactly one 0xCE primitive (8 edge + 16 shade + 16 texture). Facility reports 0 and 0 because its environment row sets clouds=0 (bgfog.c:131) and sky.c:320 takes the fill-rectangle path instead - Facility structurally CANNOT witness the sky path and is never a control for it. THE TRAP, and it cost a wrong first fix: an RDP 'triangle' is not necessarily a triangle. It carries three independent edges - major H over YH..YL, minor M over YH..YM, minor L over YM..YL - so when the minor pair is not collinear the primitive rasterises a TRAPEZOID. skyRenderFull uses this deliberately, setting XH to the left screen edge and XM to the right with zero slopes (sky.c:2209,:2212) to cover the whole sky band with ONE command; it has two triangle headers in an if/else but only one shade and one texture block, so 40 words describe a four-cornered shape. Decoding it as three vertices drew half the band and left the rest showing the backdrop, which still looked like 'Dam has no sky'. Walk the boundary as a polygon; a genuine triangle falls out of the same code as a degenerate case. METHOD note worth more than the bug: the first A/B looked like a 3.8% pixel win and was almost entirely the level-title CAPTION appearing in one run and not the other - the sky band itself had moved 827 pixels by a mean of 7. Counting differing pixels across a whole frame is not evidence that the thing you changed changed; band the diff to the region under test, and look at the image.  2026-09-08, B-101, ED rdp_setscissor: ucode05.txt gives the layout in full - ulx 0x00FFF000 / uly 0x00000FFF in the upper word, lrx / lry likewise in the lower, all four in 10.2 fixed point. That was enough to decode the per-room portal box without reading any decomp. What the notes do NOT say, and what no file in the corpus answers, is whether the RDP's scissor is load-bearing for the IMAGE on a port that already has a depth buffer - see not_covered. Measured instead: honouring it changes nothing at all on dam and depot (232 sampled frames of recorded play, zero pixels), and on frigate it REMOVES an 11x199 framebuffer band of ship structure, so it is not the safe no-op it looks like.  2026-09-08, opcode 06 - CALL versus BRANCH, and the reason an F8 bug mark described a third of the frame it claimed to cover. ucode05.txt:243-244 gives the two forms of the display-list command in two lines - `xx00xxxx push display list` and `xx01xxxx branch to display list` - and :437-440 (B8 rsp_enddl) completes them: "If the current list was called by an 06 command, returns from branch." So a PUSH suspends the running list and resumes it after the 06, consuming a stack level; a BRANCH REPLACES the running list, which never resumes, and consumes none. A branch target is a SIBLING of the list it replaced, not a child of it, and the distinction is not cosmetic: MEASURED on a dam-seam-02 replay at room 111, one frame took six chained tail transfers and reached call-level 1 while sl_gfx_dl.c's walk() - which recurses for both forms - reached recursion depth 7. 1 + 6 = 7 exactly, so the walker's depth is its own branch count and nothing about the game's list. walk() refuses to descend past 8, and refused=0 on every frame of every run measured, so the cap has never fired - but the margin is one more chained transfer, and it is the BRANCH conflation that consumes it. WHAT IT COST: the mark table recorded submissions only at depth 0, and the frame's content lives under the transfers. On that same frame 95 of 136 submissions and 2311 of 3517 triangles - two thirds of the frame, including room 113's geometry and 62 segment-5 lists - were below the gate and could never appear. Triangle COUNTS still reconciled, because everything inside a transfer was tallied against it, which is exactly what made a truncated table look whole. A count that reconciles is not evidence of coverage; the table has to say what its own coverage was.  2026-09-10, B-108, the Dam water's spatial frequency: ucode05_old.txt's F5 mask fields (mask s 0x000000F0, mask t 0x0003C000) are the WRAP PERIOD exponents and the same entry's tmem/line give the ROW STRIDE, and the two are INDEPENDENT quantities a tile may set differently. src/game/unk_092E50.c's water tiles are the witness: CI8 line=2 (16 texels a row) under masks=maskt=5 (wrap at 32), so the RDP's visible 32x32 period is a 16-byte-stride walk of the 1024-byte source - each sampled row is 32 CONSECUTIVE bytes starting at t*16, successive rows overlapping by half, which is just what TMEM addressing t*line+s says. B-102 read the stride as the width and B-088 read the mask as both; each is right about ONE quantity. Sizing the GL repeat from the stride made Sightline wrap S at 16 texels where the RDP wraps at 32 - measured at the owner's mark 20260910-070752/mark-001: the water span s[-158.66,552.19] texels is 22.2 RDP periods and was drawn as 44.4, exactly 2x too dense in S while T (mask 32, height 32) was right. The fix (SL_TILE_PERIOD, default on): period = 2^mask on a wrapping masked axis, decode rows at the tile's line stride; the two coincide on every ordinary texture (B-077 measured that equality on Facility), and the 64-state texprobe census at the mark changed nothing but the water. ALSO measured, and easy to misread: the F3 for this load names 512 texels at siz=2 - 16-BIT units, 1024 bytes of CI8 indices with the TLUT at +0x400 - so the source has 64 stride-rows and the 32x32 window's last row (bytes 496..527) is real data, not an overflow. 2026-09-13, B-128 - the tracer's rainbow (Gitea #16). `7F076D68 - generate DL for ImgDecl.txt` answered twice more: :982-987 `tmem += tilesize` per level is the authority that a mip chain is ONE loadblock with tiles 1..n at word offsets INSIDE it (so a tmem address is a RANGE query, not a start-match - the native map matched starts only and answered the flare's tile 1 with the treeline strip an earlier draw had loaded at word 128), and the per-depth line rule gives the word size: 'width to nearest word' = (width+3)>>2 for 16-bit (:885-890) AND 32-bit (:870-875), 8-bit (:900-905) >>3, 4-bit (:915-920) >>4 - so a 64-bit tmem word holds 4 texels at 32bpp too, i.e. 16 DRAM bytes per word (gbi.h:431 G_IM_SIZ_32b_LINE_BYTES=2 against :430 _BYTES=4 is the same fact). The corpus is otherwise silent on tmem itself (grep -rni tmem over the notes: only the F5 tmem field, ucode05.txt:751 / ucode05_old.txt:965, and the generators' use of it). See docs/backlog.md B-128.

setup-objects.learned: PROPDEF_CCTV=6 and PROPDEF_AUTOGUN=13 cross-check against 'type 06 camera' and '0D autoturrets'. The 'Action Block Types.txt' word-count table is the authority on RECORD LENGTH, and bondtypes.h is not: sizepropdef() reproduces that table exactly for all 47 types, but sizeof(CCTVRecord)/4 is 63 against the file's 0x3b, because the struct describes what the game READS (it reads past the record) rather than what the file holds. Every other per-type struct matches its stride - measured 2026-08-25 by dumping every sizeof against the table. Anything that WRITES a record must bound itself by the table, not by sizeof. 2026-08-25, B-033: 'object block types.txt' type 04 key annotates offset 0x80 as "lock bit values.  Door locks are masked with these values in order to open them", with the example word 00 00 00 06 - so 0x80 is a WORD, and bondtypes.h's union { s8 keyID; u32 keyflags; } at that offset is a byte VIEW of it, not the field. gen_swap.py resolves a union by its FIRST MEMBER, saw the s8, and emitted no swap, so KeyRecord.keyflags stayed wire-order while DoorRecord.keyflags (0x9c) was swapped - the AND in bondinvCheckHasKeyFlags could then never match and no keycard opened any door. The rule this yields: when a union spans a documented field, the NOTE decides the width, and the narrow member is extracted arithmetically at its read sites (keyID is the wire MSB; its only reader is propobj.c check_if_entry_is_collectable). AUTHORITY for the bg file's own section layout, and specifically for the PORTAL DATA TABLE, which settled B-099. The table at bg_file+0x8 is a list of 8-byte records: 4-byte OFFSET to portal polygonal data (mask with 0x0F000000), then connected room 1, connected room 2, two control bytes; NULL record terminates. The record and the POLYGON are separate objects and the mapping is many-to-one - several records legitimately name ONE polygon, one per pair of rooms the same opening joins (Dam has polygons with two, three and four records each; 194 records over 160 polygons). The Global Visibility Microcode section of the same note reaches those polygons by offset as well ('64000000 0Fxxxxxx  offset within file, typically to portal data'). A polygon is numPoints in the first byte, 3 filler bytes, then x/y/z floats, points clockwise, relative to stage origin - and the note states each float SHOULD BE AN INTEGER VALUE, which is a free correctness check on any decode of them. Reading the table as one-record-one-polygon is what made sl_bg_file_swap byte-swap shared polygons once per REFERENCE; an even reference count restored big-endian, the floats decoded as denormals, and every portal plane derived from them collapsed to a zero normal - so the portal was rejected as a back face forever and the room behind it was never drawn.

2026-08-25: the notes fix the format codes and depths but are SILENT on the odd-row texel swizzle - see the not_covered entry. Two codes are traps: type 2 (RGB24) is stored 32bpp 'forced to 32bit fixed alpha' and type 3 (RGB15) stored 16bpp 'with forced alpha', so both decode identically to their wide siblings rather than at their nominal depth. The 5551 and I8A8 bit splits were taken from Rare's own palette arithmetic in texShrinkPaletted (image.c), not guessed.  2026-08-25, B-027 - the crosshair's untextured white square. "image declarations.txt" gives the 0xC-byte declaration record and settles that ONLY the leading u32 is word data: 0x4 width, 0x5 height, 0x6 level, 0x7 format, 0x8 bitdepth, 0x9/0xA clamp-mirror S/T, 0xB pad are eight independent u8 fields. image_bank.c:180 was word-swapping the whole 0x1400 bank ("load global image bank.txt"), which reverses those eight bytes in two groups of four, for EVERY image in the bank - crosshair, ammo icons, explosion sprites, glass, monitors, radar, sky/water, MP icons. Measured: the crosshair's {w=0x20,h=0x20,level=0,fmt=RGBA,depth=32b} read back as {w=0,h=0,level=0x20,fmt=0x20,depth=0}, so texSelect took its level!=0 mipmap branch with lod=32 and emitted 32 settile/settilesize pairs with zero line stride and uls==lrs - a zero-area tile. The texrect itself was byte-identical before and after the fix, because gunfire.c:6263 passes 0x20,0x20 literally; only the binding was broken, which is why the square was the right size in the right place with no art. The bank is two regions, not one: the first 0xAC8 bytes are the seventeen globalDL_* lists (words - texLoadFromDisplayList's native branch needs them native), and from s_genericimage to the end it is nothing but declarations. Swap them separately. General lesson worth more than the bug: "structured data, so word-swap it" is not a valid inference - swapping at a load choke point still requires knowing the field widths there. Also: segment symbols carry the 0x02000000 segment VMA, so a bank-relative offset needs the same +0xFE000000 image_bank.c's pointer fixups already use.
  2026-08-25, B-034 - the note "Texture application (Rooms).txt" describes ROOM AND OBJECT BINARIES, and two of its rules do NOT carry over to display lists the game builds at runtime. (a) "BB000001 = on, level 0 = untextured" is a room-file convention only: measured over whole recursed Facility frames, ZERO triangles are drawn under a combiner naming no texel, and the BB.on=1/level=0 triangles carry FC121824 FF33FFFF = (TEXEL0-0)*SHADE+0. BB's level field is not a texture gate for runtime lists - do not use it as one. (b) "only four combiner settings GE ever uses" is likewise room-only; runtime lists emit at least FC121824 FF33FFFF (G_CC_MODULATEIA), FC26A004 1F1093FF / 1FFC93FC / 1F1493FF (G_CC_TRILERP + G_CC_MODULATEIA2, the 2-cycle mip path) and FC159804 5FFEDBF8 = (TEXEL0-ENV)*SHADE_A+ENV, model.c's Type3 "GunLighting" branch. Also measured the same day: the C0 image-recall pseudo-command the declarations note documents never reaches a submitted list - the game expands it into real FD/F5/F3/F0 first - so a DL interpreter needs no C0 case. And the first-person viewmodel is ~100% paletted CI with 6-level mip chains (18/18 render tiles fmt=2, 56 F0 loadtluts per frame) while the surrounding Facility world is mostly IA/I with zero TLUT loads, which is the discriminator whenever the arm and hand look wrong and the world does not. 2026-08-25, B-041: 'huffman compression types.txt' carries the SEVEN VALUE TABLES indexed by img_type 0-C, and two of them must not be confused. #4 is the BITCOUNT IN THE COMPRESSED STREAM (type 0=0x20, type 2=0x18, type 3=0x0F); #6 is the N64 PIXEL SIZE of the DECOMPRESSED buffer (type 0=32bit, type 2=32bit, type 3=16bit). So type 2 is 24 bits per pixel compressed and 32bpp once expanded 'forced to 32bit fixed alpha', and type 3 is 15 bits compressed and 16bpp expanded. src/gfx/sl_gfx_tex.h's 'stored 32bpp' for RGB24 describes the DECOMPRESSED form and is right; reading #4 as the stored size would make it look wrong. #5 gives the N64 image type per code and #7 'imageflip values for indexed types' (nonzero only for codes 9-C) is not modelled anywhere in this tree. 2026-09-04, B-090 - texSelect (src/game/othermodemicrocode.c) had NO mapped area at all, so an investigation into the gun-barrel shadow reached for the decomp first; it picks format/depth/combiner/render mode for EVERY textured draw and is now mapped here. A METHOD correction worth more than the mapping: gedocs.py 'search' matches FILENAMES ONLY, so 'search shadow' and 'search imgdecl' both returned no matches while 'image declarations.txt' and 'imageTypes.txt' - already listed in this very area - answered both at once. Reading those absences as corpus silence would have been another instance of the error rule 7 warns about; use 'for <file>' or grep the corpus before claiming silence. WHAT THEY SETTLED: 'image declarations.txt' confirms the 0xC-byte record field-for-field (0x7 format, 0x8 bitdepth), so the decomp struct is right; and 'imageTypes.txt', a per-image-ID inventory, gives 07BC - the shadow blob under Bond in the gun-barrel walk - as Type 460B Paletted with BD colours [W20 H20] 8-Bit coloured Paletted Transparent, i.e. CI8 32x32 with alpha, matching the measured 32x32 exactly. The declaration nevertheless carries format=0 (RGBA) with bitdepth=1 (8b), an illegal RDP pair, because the authoritative format lives in the texture POOL (tex->gbiformat) and texSelect's texFindInPool MISSES here: Bond's intro textures load into a STACK-LOCAL texpool (title.c:475) while texSelect searches the global one. That is Rare's own code with no ifdef, so the cartridge emits RGBA/8b too and never loads a TLUT (texSelect loads a palette only when format==2). Measured consequence natively: gbi_to_sl_fmt returns -1 for RGBA/8b, tile_texture reports TR_FMT, tex_apply disables GL_TEXTURE_2D, and the quad paints the combiner's white shade at vertex alpha 0x50 over G_RM_CLD_SURF2 - which is the light patch under Bond. answers.element specifier: p180/p207 state it is the BYTE element of the vector register, not the ordinal element index used by the computational ops - the two conventions differ and mixing them is an easy error
answers.effective address: per-instruction; the encoded offset is scaled by the access width (LDV p180: source offset must be a multiple of 8 and is stored shifted right by 3). Address is masked to 12 bits (DMEM size)
answers.boundary behaviour: LQV p189 / SQV p219 transfer only from the address up to the enclosing 16-byte boundary, with LRV p190 / SRV p224 covering the remainder; Figure 3-2 p51 is the picture. LDV p180 / SDV p207 are plain 64-bit transfers with no such truncation described
answers.load delay: vector loads have three delay slots; hardware interlocks if the target is used sooner (p180, p189)
